incidents.name: StoneVault unprotected round settlement
incidents.notes: StoneVault's round-advance entry point (selector 0x5069fb57) had no access control, so the attacker could deposit, settle the round themselves at a share price they had just moved, and withdraw at a profit in the same transaction.

sources.ref: onchain review: StoneVault 0xA62F9C5af106FeEE069F38dE51098D9d81B90572 (holding STONE 0x7122985656e38BDC0302Db86685bb972b145bD3C, StakeStone Ether) created 2023-09-24T06:20:23Z by 0xc1364ad857462e1b60609d9e56b5e24c5c21a312, unrelated to the attack sender; no EIP-1967 events, age from deployment (44.7 days). ~17 ETH x $1,886.72 at incidentTimestamp 1699400627 (DefiLlama) = $32,074. Recheck (deployment basis confirmed): keccak(eth_getCode) on StoneVault is identical at the creation block 18203833 and the incident block 18523441, no EIP-1967 or beacon slot is set, the exploit trace contains no DELEGATECALL out of the vault, and the single 0xf4 byte in the runtime lies inside trailing constant data rather than reachable code, so the vault's executing code is immutable.
